reference: Outside the house: energy average over every outside wall, 0.4 m out, window height. LAeq per local hour. Event peaks (event_lmax_dba, audible_per_hour) are at the wall facing the event; an event is audible when its peak beats the hour's steady total.

data.weather: Open-Meteo historical archive (ERA5), 2025: hourly temperature and rain

caveats: Traffic counts (TxDOT AADT) for South Braeswood Boulevard, South Post Oak Road, South Post Oak Road Frontage Road, West Loop South, West Loop South Frontage Road; other roads use typical volumes for their class. Hours follow a typical weekday.
Rail uses default freight traffic (12 trains a day), not counts; horns at crossings are not included.
Background (quiet suburban residential) stands for unmodelled sound: distant city, AC units, insects. Aircraft are not modelled.
Neighbouring buildings come from OpenStreetMap, which misses some houses; a built-up allowance covers the rest. Expect about +/-3 dB.
Animal sound levels come from typical published values and calling densities per habitat, not from recordings at this house. Expect +/-5 dB, more for frogs (they depend on the weather of the week).
Horn and dog-barking rates are assumptions (see soundscape.json); their levels per event are typical values.
The residual background already stands for some insects and birds; with the nature sources on top it errs loud.
Not modelled: aircraft (Hobby airport is about 13 km away), helicopters, train horns at crossings, construction, lawn equipment, AC condensers next door, wind in the trees.
